AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 20, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8082-013-905; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Department of the Air Force; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of

  V.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE 54956.9(d)(2): Significant exposure to litigation in 1 case.

  VI. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE 54956.9(d)(4): Initiation of litigation in 1 case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Debbie Binggeli
  Norwalk Church of the Nazarene

FLAG SALUTE
  Karla Barboza
  Norwalk High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to Recognize the Los Angeles County Library for being the 2019 Library of the Year and Norwalk
  Library for Celebrating its 50th Anniversary in the Civic Center Plaza.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  National Night Out Highlights.

  2.  Norwalk Town Square Mural Unveiling.
   3.  Athens Services, One Year of Service.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  August 6 and 13, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period July 14, 2019 – July 27,
  2019, in the total amount of $1,014,482.93. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  31, 2019 – August 13, 2019, in the total amount of $6,461,825.47. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – AUGUST 14, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  5.  PROJECT NO. 7798-R - APPROVAL OF PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AND AUTHORIZATION TO
  ADVERTISE FOR THE REHABILITATION OF GERDES PARK PARKING LOT, PROJECT NO. 7798-
  R, ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 19-14 - Staff recommends City Council approve plans and
  specifications for rehabilitation of Gerdes Park parking lot, Project No. 7798-R, authorize advertisement
  for bids, and set a bid opening date of September 19, 2019. 1005-04-7798

  Report

  6.  FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the proposed project for JAG grant submission, and allocate available 2019 JAG funds for the
  continued lease of Mobile Digital Computers and training of Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department
  personnel for National Incident-Based Reporting System compliance. 730-03-09

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 – W.G. ZIMMERMAN ENGINEERING, INC. – DESIGNATION OF
  INTERIM CITY ENGINEER - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the
  agreement with W.G. Zimmerman Engineering, Inc. to designate Glen Kau as the Interim City
  Engineer; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment provided there is funding in the
  budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 310-02

  Report

  8.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK – REPLACE PARKING LOT GATE FOR SARA MENDEZ PARK -
  Staff recommends City Council confirm emergency work to replace the parking lot gate at Sara
  Mendez Park completed by Perez Fence Company in the amount of $4,800.00. 955

  Report

  9.  AGREEMENTS - ASSIGNMENT OF NON-CONSUMPTIVE WATER USE PERMITS TO CONTINUE
  GROUNDWATER REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES AT THE FORMER NORWALK DEFENSE FUEL
  SUPPLY POINT - Staff recommends City Council approve the agreements with Santa Fe Pacific
  Pipeline, L.P., on behalf of Kinder Morgan Energy Partners and Defense Logistics Agency for
   Assignment of Non-Consumptive Water Use Permits for the continued groundwater remediation
  activities at the Tank Farm; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements and any
  amendments, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 935-01

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

THIS ITEM IS BEING CONTINUED TO SEPTEMBER 3, 2019 AND WILL BE RE-NOTICED.

  11. PETITION FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE – RESOLUTION NO. 19-49
  – SOUTH SIDE OF THE 11000 BLOCK OF EXCELSIOR DRIVE, BETWEEN STUDEBAKER ROAD
  AND ELMCROFT AVENUE - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-49, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS
  FINDING OF FACT AND APPROVING THE INSTALLATION OF THE PREFERENTIAL PARKING
  ZONE FOR THE SOUTH END OF THE 11000 BLOCK OF EXCELSIOR DRIVE BETWEEN
  STUDEBAKER ROAD AND ELMCROFT AVENUE. 1050-02-02

  Report

REPORTS

  12. AGREEMENT - PROJECT MANAGEMENT FOR PROCUREMENT OF BATTERY ELECTRIC BUS
  AND CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with
  The LeFlore Group, LCC in the amount of $130,810 for Project Management for Procurement of
  Battery Electric Bus and Charging Infrastructure; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  13. AMENDING TITLES OF SEVERAL POSITIONS IN THE PUBLIC SERVICES DEPARTMENT - Staff
  recommends City Council approve: Staff recommends City Council approve:

  a.  title changes for the following positions: Director of Public Services to Director of Public
  Services/City Engineer, City Engineer to Principal Civil Engineer, and Utility Projects Manager to
  Senior Civil Engineer; and

  b.  direct staff to bring back a resolution to amend the Fiscal Year 2019/20 salary schedule to reflect
  the proposed changes. 135-03

  Report

  14. AMENDMENT NO. 8 – BUCKNAM AND ASSOCIATES FOR WATER SYSTEM SERVICES - Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 8 to the agreement with Bucknam and Associates
  to provide additional services and additional compensation in the amount of $48,200 for FY 2019/20.
  1070-05

  Report

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 19-50 – OPTING OUT OF THE CALIFORNIA CONGESTION MANAGEMENT
  PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-50, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING TO OPT-OUT OF THE CALIFORNIA
  CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM. 1050-01

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
 ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated August 16, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
